Issues.Title: Maximize AutoML log-loss reduction
Issues.Body:
Fixes #7839.

`MultiClassMetricManager` currently minimizes `LogLossReduction`, so AutoML prefers a lower reduction even though a higher value is better. Mark it as a maximizing metric, consistent with the existing multiclass metrics agent.

Add deterministic coverage through `SetMulticlassClassificationMetric`: verify all five optimization directions, then use three fixed trial scores to check that LogLossReduction selects the highest score while LogLoss selects the lowest. The seven new cases produce two failures before the fix and all pass afterward. No public API or TopKAccuracy evaluation changes are included.

The full repository build was not validated locally: the machine lacks the required Spectre C++ libraries, and pretrained-image downloads stalled. For the focused managed tests, native dependencies were built locally with Spectre mitigation disabled and unused image downloads were skipped with a local MSBuild import. No build configuration changes are included in this PR.

Issues.Title: Throw ArgumentNullException from DataFrame binary operators when the DataFrame is null
Issues.Body:
Fixes #5677

The scalar operators on `DataFrame` (`df + 1`, `1 + df`, `df << 1`, etc.) call straight into the instance method, so passing a null `DataFrame` throws a `NullReferenceException` from inside the library. As suggested in the triage comment, these now throw `ArgumentNullException` with `ParamName` set to `df`.

The `bool` overload mentioned in the issue no longer exists, since `bool` is excluded from the numeric operators, but every other operator overload had the same problem.

Changes:
- `DataFrame.BinaryOperators.tt`: add a null check on `df` to the three operator templates (scalar, reverse scalar and shift).
- `DataFrame.BinaryOperators.cs`: the matching change in the generated file, applied to all 112 operators. The only differences from the existing file are the added checks.
- New test `TestBinaryOperatorsWithNullDataFrame` covers the arithmetic, reverse and shift operators with a null `DataFrame`.

No public API is added or changed. Only the exception type thrown for a null argument is different.

Testing:
- Before the fix, the new test failed with `NullReferenceException`. After the fix, it passes.
- `dotnet test test/Microsoft.Data.Analysis.Tests` (net8.0, macOS arm64): 1779 passed, 6 skipped, 0 failed.
- `dotnet format whitespace --verify-no-changes` on the changed files: clean.

Issues.Title: Disable copy hard links in code coverage builds
Issues.Body:
Disable copy hard links for coverage builds to keep Coverlet's instrumented assemblies and PDBs separate from the original build outputs.

The coverage pipeline already omitted `CreateHardLinksForCopyLocalIfPossible=True`, but still unconditionally enabled `CreateHardLinksForCopyFilesToOutputDirectoryIfPossible=True`. This can make the `obj` and `bin` PDB paths refer to the same underlying file.

Coverlet rewrites assemblies and PDBs during instrumentation. Instrumenting one project's output can therefore lock the original PDB while another project reads it, a likely cause of the recurring file-access failures.

## Changes

- Explicitly set both copy hard-link options to `False` for coverage builds.
- Preserve the existing build command and hard-link settings for non-coverage jobs.
- Leave native/publish linking and test parallelism unchanged.

The trade-off is increased disk usage and copy I/O in the coverage job, without serialising test execution.

Fixes #7417

Issues.Title: AutoML MulticlassClassificationExperiment minimizes LogLossReduction — MultiClassMetricManager.IsMaximize returns false for it
Issues.Body:
## Defect

`src/Microsoft.ML.AutoML/AutoMLExperiment/IMetricManager.cs`, `MultiClassMetricManager.IsMaximize`:

```csharp
MulticlassClassificationMetric.LogLoss => false,
MulticlassClassificationMetric.LogLossReduction => false,   // should be true
```

Log-loss reduction is `1 - LogLoss / LogLoss(prior)` — higher is better (1 = perfect, 0 = no better than the class prior, negative = worse). With `IsMaximize == false` the trial loss is the metric itself and the experiment's best run is the minimum, so an experiment optimizing it returns the model that learned least.

## Reproduction (Microsoft.ML 5.0.1 / Microsoft.ML.AutoML 0.23.1, osx-arm64)

150 rows, 3 classes, one feature that separates them almost perfectly (`a = class + U(0,1)`), `MulticlassExperimentSettings.OptimizingMetric = LogLossReduction`, 10 s budget:

- trials: FastTreeOva 0.0016 → 0.4176, FastForestOva **0.9606**, LbfgsMaximumEntropy 0.6961, … then the tuner settles on SdcaMaximumEntropy at **−0.599** for the rest of the budget
- returned best: macro accuracy 0.333, log loss 1.0986 (= ln 3), log-loss reduction **0.0**
- same data with `OptimizingMetric = LogLoss`: macro accuracy 1.0, log-loss reduction 1.0

## Expected

`LogLossReduction => true`.

## Related observation (not a defect claim)

`TopKAccuracy` as an optimizing metric: the experiment evaluates with the default `topKPredictionCount = 0`, for which `MulticlassClassificationMetrics.TopKAccuracy` is 0 for every model (measured: micro accuracy 1, top-k accuracy 0). `MulticlassExperimentSettings` has no setting to pass K, so optimizing it compares constants.

Issues.Title: Fix DataFrame GroupBy Min, Max, Product and Sum aggregations
Issues.Body:
The row-subset overloads of the numeric `Min`, `Max`, `Product` and `Sum` computations (the ones `GroupBy` uses) had several problems:

- `Product(rows)` started from `default`, so it always returned 0.
- None of them checked the null bitmap, so nulls were treated as their zero-filled storage (e.g. `Min` of `[5, null]` returned 0).
- An empty or all-null selection returned `MaxValue`/`MinValue`/0 instead of null.
- `DateTime` `Min(rows)`/`Max(rows)` initialized a nullable result to null and compared against it with lifted operators, so they always returned null.

Changes:

- `PrimitiveDataFrameColumnComputations.tt`: the row-subset `Min`/`Max`/`Sum`/`Product` now skip null rows (reading the matching null bitmap buffer). `Min`/`Max`/`Sum` return null when no valid value was seen, the same as the whole-column overloads. `Product` starts from 1 and, like the whole-column `Product`, returns 1 for an empty selection. I regenerated `PrimitiveDataFrameColumnComputations.cs` from the template.
- `DateTimeComputation.cs`: `Min(rows)`/`Max(rows)` now track a `hasValue` flag and skip nulls, like the whole-column versions.

I left the existing `checked` arithmetic in the row-subset overloads alone. Because `Product` now returns real values, the existing `TestGroupBy` needed an update: it had asserted a product of 0 for both groups. The odd group's product is 189, which overflows `sbyte`, so the test now leaves the `Sbyte` column out of that `Product` call.

The indexed `Cumulative*` issues mentioned in the issue comments are not part of this change.

Testing:

- Added `DataFrameGroupByTests.TestGroupByMinMaxProductSum`. It covers groups with nulls, positive and negative values, an all-null group, and DateTime Min/Max. It fails before the fix and passes after.
- `dotnet test test/Microsoft.Data.Analysis.Tests` (net8.0, macOS arm64): 1765 passed, 6 skipped, 0 failed.

Fixes #5704

Issues.Title: SymSGD classification test hangs on Linux ARM32 Helix
Issues.Body:
**System Information (please complete the following information):**

`TestEstimatorSymSgdClassificationTrainer` becomes runnable with accurate native-library detection, then reports `Too many args to microtask: 26!` and hangs until the 3,600-second work-item timeout. Debug also reports `malloc(): unsorted double linked list corrupted`.

After the first quarantine, [build 1643911](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1643911) reaches `TestEstimatorSymSgdInitPredictor`, which reports the same microtask error and exits 255 ([Release log](https://helix.dot.net/api/2019-06-17/jobs/a5f3557f-2ac4-47ef-a3dd-b833078677fd/workitems/Microsoft.ML.Tests/console)). Issues.Title: TensorFlow image classification tests running out of memory on Linux x64
Issues.Body:
**System Information (please complete the following information):**
- OS & Version: Ubuntu 22.04 and CentOS Stream 9 x64 Helix containers.
- ML.NET Version: PR #7833, commit `100af589f`.
- .NET Version: .NET 8, Debug and Release.

**Describe the bug**
Accurate native-library detection enables previously skipped TensorFlow tests. The process exits with code 137 during `TensorFlowImageClassificationWithExponentialLRScheduling` in Release and `TensorFlowImageClassificationBadImages` in Debug. Debug logs report peak memory up to 7.2 GB. An OOM kill is suspected, not kernel-confirmed.

**Screenshots, Code, Sample Projects**
[Ubuntu Debug log](https://helix.dot.net/api/2019-06-17/jobs/3dd9ea81-c306-4655-a8c0-e70cb5043a59/workitems/Microsoft.ML.TensorFlow.Tests/console) · [Ubuntu Release log](https://helix.dot.net/api/2019-06-17/jobs/b7513017-c96f-4c53-9973-1e01da19c7ec/workitems/Microsoft.ML.TensorFlow.Tests/console)

**Additional context**
Temporarily quarantine the six image-classification training methods (10 test cases) as a group on Linux x64, including local runs and both build configurations. This covers default training, architecture variants, learning-rate scheduling, early stopping, and bad images. Keep non-training TensorFlow tests and other platforms enabled.

Reproduced outside Helix in Ubuntu 22.04 WSL x64 with the original Release binaries, .NET 8.0.16 and two CPUs: at a 16 GiB limit, 36 tests passed with 2 existing skips (peak RSS about 14.2 GiB). At an experimental 8 GiB limit, the kernel OOM-killed `dotnet` during `BadImages`. This does not establish the actual Helix memory limit. Memory retention across tests may contribute, so individual skips may only move the failure later.

The two initial skips were honored, but [build 1643911](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1643911) was killed later in `TensorFlowImageClassification` or `TensorFlowImageClassificationEarlyStopping` ([Ubuntu Release log](https://helix.dot.net/api/2019-06-17/jobs/f9c5c2bb-6518-4b8d-aab6-2dc6cd82ac29/workitems/Microsoft.ML.TensorFlow.Tests/console)). The latest payload also OOM-kills at 8 GiB in WSL. Enabling the existing per-test GC option did not prevent the OOM, so that experiment was reverted.

With the training-group quarantine, the same 8 GiB WSL reproduction completes successfully: 26 passed and 8 reported skips (6 training methods plus 2 existing model-unavailable skips), with peak RSS about 1.26 GiB. The two quarantined theories cover multiple data rows. Linux CI still needs to rerun; this is a temporary coverage reduction, not a fix for the memory retention.
